newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore marine industry 1996 output seen down.
newsitem.headline: Singapore marine industry 1996 output seen down.

text.p: Singapore's marine industry output in 1996 was projected to have fallen 10.9 percent to S$3.14 billion, the Economic Development Board said on Thursday.
The board said said in a statement Singapore's marine sector was consolidating and focusing on higher value-added markets as tighter margins affected ship repair performance.

It said the Singapore yards reported that the number of jobs was only marginally lower in 1996 than that in 1990 and 1991, but the size of jobs per ship had fallen by five to 10 percent. Margins per job had declined by one to two percent compared to the same period, it added.
The statement said a weak worldwide ship repair market was another factor in the fall, along with strong competition from repair yards in the Middle East.
Other factors include price competition among local yards and the strength of the Singapore dollar against the U.S. dollar, the currency in which deals are made, the EDB said.
The EDB had projected a 10 percent growth for the marine sector in 1996.
